questions.q: A plane electromagnetic wave of frequency <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>MHz</mi></math> propagates in free space along <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>-direction. At a particular space and time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>E</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mover><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo> </mo></mrow><mo>^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. What is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>B</mi><mo>→</mo></mover></math> at this point?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
It is given that 

 E→=6.6j^( V m-1).

The relation between the electric, magnetic field and speed of light is E→×B→=c→.

Clearly, B→=B0(k^)

Using the relation,
     cB0=E
⇒B0=Ec=6.63×108=2.2×10-8 T

questions.q: An electromagnetic wave is represented by the electric filed <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></mrow><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">sin</mi></mrow><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ω</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mo>+</mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>6</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>z</mi></mrow></mfenced></mrow></mfenced><mo>.</mo></mrow></mrow></math> Taking unit vectors in <math><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></math> and <math><mi>z</mi></math> directions to be <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi></math> the directions of propogations <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo></math> is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The standard equation of electromagnetic wave E→=E0n^sinωt-kx^

here x^ represents the direction of propagation wave.

On comparing the given equation with the standard equation, the direction of propagation is along line -6y+8z . Thus, unit vector along the direction of propagation is,
s^=-6j^+8k^10=-35j^+45k^

questions.q: The electric field in an electromagnetic wave is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>56</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>sin</mi><mi>ω</mi><mfenced><mfrac><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mi>c</mi></mfrac></mfenced><msup><mi>NC</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Find the intensity of the wave if it is propagating along <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>-axis in the free space. (Given <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>85</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given, E=56.5sinωt-xc N C-1

Comparing it with the general equation of electromagnetic wave, 

E=E0sin ωt-kx

We have, E0=56.5 N C-1

So, the intensity will be I=12ε0E02c

=12×8.85×10-12×56.52×3×108

=4.24  W m-2

questions.q: The magnetic field of a plane electromagnetic wave is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>B</mi><mo mathvariant="italic">→</mo></mover><mo mathvariant="italic">=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo mathvariant="italic">-</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></msup><mi>sin</mi><mfenced close="]" open="["><mrow><mn>200</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo mathvariant="italic">+</mo><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfenced><mover><mi>i</mi><mo mathvariant="italic">^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> . Where, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>c</mi><mo mathvariant="italic">=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> is the speed of light the corresponding electric filed is :

questions.solution:
E0=cB0

∴E→×B→‖C→⇒k^×i^=j^

E→=3×108×3×10-8sin[200πy+ct(-k^)  =9sin[200πy+ct](-k^)

questions.q: An object is placed in a medium of refractive index <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math>. An electromagnetic wave of intensity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>8</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> falls normally on the object and it is absorbed completely. The radiation pressure on the object would be (speed of light in free space <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>8</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> ):
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the radiation pressure is given by

P=Iv   ...1

Also, the velocity of the electromagnetic wave can be expressed as

μ=cv   ...2

Equations (1) and (2) imply that

P=I·μc=6×108×33×108=6 N m-2

questions.q: Intensity of sunlight is observed as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>092</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi>Wm</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> at a point in free space. What will be the peak value of magnetic field at that point ? <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi>ε</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>85</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>12</mn><mo> </mo></mrow></msup><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Iavg =B02C2μ0&1μ0=ϵ0C2
I=B022ϵ0C3
 B0=2Iϵ0C3
 B0=2.77×10-8 T

questions.q: A point source of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi></math> emits light with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>%</mo></math> efficiency. At a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> from the source, the intensity produced by the electric field component is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Total power emitted =100×5100=5 W

Now intensity due to electric field will be half of the total intensity. Therefore,

IE=12×powerarea=12×54π×52

=140πWm2

questions.q: The energy associated with electric field is <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>U</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>E</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></math> and with magnetic field is <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>U</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></math> for an electromagnetic wave in free space. Then:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The average energy density of electric field is given by

uE=12εE02

Here, E0 is the maximum value of electric field.

The average energy density of magnetic field is given by

uB=B022μ

Here, B0 is the maximum value of magnetic field.

The speed of light is given by c2=1με

Also, E0=cB0

So, uE=12c2μcB02=B022μ=uB

As the energy density of electric field and magnetic field are equal, the energy associated for equal volume will also be equal.

questions.q: The magnetic field of a plane electromagnetic wave is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>B</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></msup><mi>sin</mi><mfenced><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>11</mn></msup><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfenced><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math>. The amplitude of the electric field would be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The ratio of electric field amplitude to the magnetic field amplitude of an electromagnetic wave is equal to the speed of light in the medium. Therefore,

c=E0B0⇒E0=cB0

⇒E0=3×108×2×10-8

⇒E0=6 V m-1

According to the given equation B→=2×10-8sin0.5×103x+1.5×1011tj^ T the wave travels in x direction. As electric field and magnetic field vibrate perpendicular to the velocity of light, electric field can not be along x axis.

questions.q: A plane electromagnetic wave of frequency <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>35</mn><mo> </mo><mi>MHz</mi></math> travels in free space along the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi></math>-direction. At a particular point (in space and time) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>E</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The value of magnetic field at this point is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At every instant, the ratio of the magnitude of the electric field to the magnitude of the magnetic field in an electromagnetic wave equals the speed of light.

Therefore, EB=c

⇒EB=3×108

⇒B=E3×108=9.63×108

⇒B=3.2×10-8 T

Now, direction of magnetic field can be calculated as

B^=v^×E^

=i^×j^=k^

So, B→=3.2×10-8k^T

questions.q: The electric fields of two plane electromagnetic plane waves in vacuum are given by <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mi>E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">cos</mi></mrow><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>k</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfenced></mrow></mrow></math> and <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mi>E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">cos</mi></mrow><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>k</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow></mfenced></mrow></mrow></math> At <math><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo></math> a particle of charge <math><mi>q</mi></math> is at origin with a velocity <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>08</mn><mi>c</mi><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>^</mo></mover></math> ( <math><mi>c</mi></math> is the speed of light in vaccum). The instantaneous force experienced by the particle is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Magnetic field vectors associated with this electromagnetic wave are given by
B→1=E0ck^cos⁡kx-ωt & B→2=E0ci^cos⁡ky-ωt
F→=qE→+qV→×B→
=qE→1+E→2+qV→×B→1+B→2
By putting the value of E→1,E→2,B→1&B→2
The net Lorentz force on the charged particles is
F→=qE00.8cos⁡kx-ωti^+cosky-ωtj^+0.2cosky-ωtk^
At t=0 and at x=y=0
F→=qE00.8i^+j^+0.2k^

questions.q:
In an electromagnetic wave, the electric field vector and magnetic field vector are given as E→=E0i^ and B→=B0k^, respectively. The direction of
propagation of electromagnetic wave is along:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Direction of propagation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mover><mi>E</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>×</mo><mover><mi>B</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>×</mo><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math>.

questions.q: In an electromagnetic wave, at an instant and at a particular position, the electric field is along the negative z-axis and magnetic field is along the positive x-axis. Then the direction of propagation of electromagnetic wave is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Direction of propagation of the electromagnetic wave is along E →×B→

Thus,

n→=E-k^×Bi^

Therefore,

n^=-k^×i^=-j^

questions.q: A plane EM wave is propagating along $x$ direction. It has a wavelength of $4 \mathrm{~mm}$. If electric field is in $y$ direction with the maximum magnitude of $60 \mathrm{Vm}^{-1}$, the equation for magnetic field is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{E}=\mathrm{BC} \Rightarrow 60=\mathrm{B} \times 3 \times 10^8\Rightarrow \mathrm{B}=2 \times 10^{-7}$
Also $\quad \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{f} \lambda\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 3 \times 10^8=\mathrm{f} \times 4 \times 10^{-3} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}=\frac{3}{4} \times 10^{11} \\ & \Rightarrow \omega=2 \pi \mathrm{f}=\frac{3}{4} \times 2 \pi \times 10^{11} \\ & \Rightarrow \omega=\frac{\pi}{2} \times 10^3 \mathrm{C}\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad$ Electric field $\Rightarrow y$ direction
Propagation $\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}$ direction
Magnetic field $\Rightarrow \mathrm{z}$-direction

questions.q: Sun light falls normally on a surface of area <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>36</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> and exerts an average force of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>7</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> within a time period of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn></math> minutes. Considering a case of complete absorption, the energy flux of incident light is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The radiation pressure in case of complete absorption is given by,

P=Ic.

Therefore, the force will be,

F=Ic×A⇒I=FcA

⇒I=7.2×10-9×3×10836×10-4=600 W m-2⇒I=0.06 W cm-2

questions.q:
If the magnetic field of a plane electromagnetic wave is given by (The speed of light =3×108 m/s)

questions.q:
A beam of light travelling along X-axis is described by the electric field Ey=900sinωt-xc. The ratio of electric force to magnetic force on a charge q moving along Y-axis with a speed of 3×107 m s-1 will be :

[Given speed of light =3×108 m s-1 ]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given, Ey=900sinωt-ωxc

Here, E0=900

Electric field and electric force are related as FE=qE0

Magnetic force of a moving charge is given by FB=qvB0

Thus, the ratio FEFB=E0vB0

Using relation between magnetic and electric field, we have

FEFB=cv=3×1083×107=10:1

questions.q: In the given electromagnetic wave $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{y}}=600 \sin (\omega \mathrm{t}-\mathrm{kx}) \mathrm{Vm}^{-1}$, intensity of the associated light beam is (in $\mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^2$ : (Given $\epsilon_0=9 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{C}^2 \mathrm{~N}^{-1} \mathrm{~m}^{-2}$ )

questions.q: A linearly polarised electromagnetic wave in vacuum is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>cos</mi><mfenced open="[" close="]"><mrow><mfenced><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></mfenced><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mfenced><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow></mfenced><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfenced><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> is incident normally on a perfectly reflecting wall at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></math>. Choose the correct option.

questions.q: The ratio of average electric energy density and total average energy density of electromagnetic wave is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Average electric energy density is stated as uE=12ε0E2

Total average energy density U= 12ε0E2+12μ0B2

=12ε0E2+12μ0E2c2    (As B=Ec)

=12ε0E2+12μ0E2ε0μ0=12ε0E2+12E2ε0=ε0E2

Hence, the ratio, uEU=12.
